subject: Request: SLA variance & order form language for Medico enterprise MSA
messages:
From: Amira Soliman <amira@medico.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.inference.com
Cc: contracts@medico.com
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: SLA variance & order form language for Medico enterprise MSA

Hi Sean,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited about Redwood's latency profiles and the KV caching approach. We're working through our internal procurement and legal checklist for the enterprise MSA + order form. Two items came up that I wanted to surface early so we can avoid surprises during redlines: 

1) Uptime/Availability: Medico's legal team requires a 99.99% monthly availability commitment for production endpoints in-scope for Rx processing. We understand your standard is 99.9% for hosted; can Redwood provide a tailored addendum that either (a) commits to 99.99% for a dedicated pool or (b) documents an agreed set of exceptions and a remediation cadence?

2) Latency SLOs: Our product team wants an upper-bound p95 token latency for the model family we're discussing (gpt-11-lite family) under baseline traffic. If you can provide suggested order form language that maps the SLA to the dedicated capacity configuration, that would help our procurement write the purchase order.

If helpful, I've attached a short redline from our side that shows the sections where we expect higher scrutiny (section 3.2 uptime, section 4.1 remedies). Can you route this to your legal and platform leads? We're targeting signature in September and would like to avoid multiple rounds of back-and-forth on the availability definition.

Attachments: Medico_SLA_Requirements_Summary.pdf (PDF stub)

Thanks,
Amira Soliman
Head of Procurement
Medico Health
amira@medico.com
(415) 555-0129

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.inference.com
To: Amira Soliman <amira@medico.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.inference.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference.com
Date: Mon, 9 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA variance & order form language for Medico enterprise MSA

Hi Amira — thanks for the clear note and the sample redline. Appreciate surfacing this early.

Quick summary of next steps from our side:
- I'm looping in Laura (legal) and Vivek (platform/solutions) so they can propose language and a pragmatic approach for production guarantees.
- We can offer a dedicated capacity order form with a 99.99% target availability for the dedicated pool, but there are a few standard carve-outs we need to call out (force majeure, customer-managed network issues, scheduled maintenance windows, and third-party infra incidents). Laura will propose concrete carve-out text and a remediation/credit table.
- For latency, Vivek will draft p95 token latency guidance tied to the dedicated GPU class and sequence-length profile. We usually map SLOs to a configured 'profile' in the order form (e.g., Dedicated-XL, 2x KV cache) and include a verification run during onboarding.

Can you confirm the contract owner on your side for the MSA (legal or procurement)? Also, do you have a preferred schedule for the remediation SLAs (time-to-detect, time-to-recover) — e.g., 4 hours to acknowledge, 72 hours target for a full resolution for production outages?

I'll get back with draft language by tomorrow EOD PT.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
(628) 555-0199
sean_gallagher@redwood.inference.com

From: laura_bennett@redwood.inference.com
To: Amira Soliman <amira@medico.com>, sean_gallagher@redwood.inference.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA variance & order form language for Medico enterprise MSA

Hi Amira / Sean — looping in legal with a short draft and our recommended remediation table. Attached are three docs: a proposed SLA addendum (Medico_SLA_Addendum_Draft.docx), a recommended order form section that ties SLOs to the Dedicated-XL config (OrderForm_LineItem_Pricing.xlsx), and an excerpt of our SOC2 evidence starter pack (SOC2_AWS_Audit_STUB.pdf).

Key points in this draft (high level):
- Availability target: We can commit to 99.99% monthly availability for a Dedicated-XL pool when customer signs a 12-month reserved capacity order and enables cross-region active-active replica. The addendum includes the qualification criteria and a runbook for verifying availability during onboarding.
- Carve-outs: Standard carve-outs for third-party network providers, customer-controlled credentials/networking, and scheduled maintenance (we propose a 6-hour monthly scheduled maintenance cap and notification windows).
- Remedies: For unplanned availability breaches, we propose a credit schedule capped at 25% of the monthly fee for the impacted order form line item; higher credits available under mutually-agreed escalation. Credits are calculated pro-rata against the impacted pool line item.
- Latency SLO: We propose a p95 token generation latency target of 350ms for the gpt-11-lite family under the Dedicated-XL config at baseline traffic (<=20 RPS). The order form language includes a verification test run within 14 days of go-live and an acceptance gating criteria.

Open asks for Medico: 
- Is Medico able to commit to the cross-region active-active requirement? If not, we should discuss the availability target and associated credits.
- Does your security team require any changes to the incident notification cadence? We currently offer 4-hour acknowledgement and a 72-hour target to resolution for severity-1 incidents for dedicated pools.

If these high-level bullets look acceptable, Sean and I can produce a redline-ready .docx that you can circulate to your legal.

--
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.inference.com

Attachment stubs:
- Medico_SLA_Addendum_Draft.docx (DOCX stub)
- OrderForm_LineItem_Pricing.xlsx (XLSX stub)
- SOC2_AWS_Audit_STUB.pdf (PDF stub)

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.inference.com
To: Amira Soliman <amira@medico.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.inference.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.inference.com
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SLA variance & order form language for Medico enterprise MSA

Amira — thanks, Laura — this looks good and is exactly the level of detail we wanted to provide. 

Summary / next steps: 
1) Sean to produce a redline-ready .docx incorporating Laura's bullets and the carve-outs by EOD PT tomorrow.
2) Medico to confirm whether cross-region active-active is acceptable (Amira to confirm with infra team).
3) If Medico accepts active-active, legal teams can run a single redline pass against the attached addendum; otherwise we'll schedule a 30-minute call to discuss trade-offs before multiple redlines.
4) I'll open a HubSpot deal note with the proposed order form line items and attach the drafts (hubspot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/9876543).

Can we lock a 30-minute slot Thursday 10–11am PT if we need it? If you confirm active-active today, we can skip the call and move straight to a document pass.

Cheers,
Sean
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
